newsitem.title: USA: US Midwest direct hogs seen steady-off $1 -dealers.
newsitem.headline: US Midwest direct hogs seen steady-off $1 -dealers.

text.p: U.S. Midwest direct cash hogs early Tuesday sold at prices steady to $1.00 per cwt lower than Monday's tops amid more than adequate hog supplies, livestock dealers and packer buyers said.
Interior Iowa and southern Minnesota hogs sold $0.50 to $1.00 per cwt lower at $53.50 to $55.00 in the country and $55.00 to $56.50 at plants.
Hog supplies reportedly were coming in numbers two percent greater than a year ago, a packer buyer said.
"At this rate, we should have four to five percent more hogs by the end of the year," he said.
Illinois hogs sold $0.50 lower at $54.50 to $55.50 in the country and $55.50 to $56.00 at plants in brisk activity.
"The phones haven't stopped ringing all morning," one Illinois dealer said.

Indiana hogs sold $0.50 to $1.00 lower at $54.00 to $54.50 in the country and $55.50 to $56.00 at plants, sources there said. At least one major packing plant in the Indiana/Ohio area also was slow in putting out bids as prices softened, they said.
Ohio hogs sold steady at $55.50 to $56.00 in the country and $56.50 to $57.00 at plants.
